title: Degree at most zero characterizes constant functions
statement: A Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ has degree $\le 0$ if and only if it is constant, that is, $f(x) = f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$.
replaced:
A Boolean function $f : \{0,1\}^n \to \{0,1\}$ has degree $\le 0$ if and only if
it is constant, i.e.\ $f(x) = f(y)$ for all $x, y \in \{0,1\}^n$.
